newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Snow White sues Disney for "stolen" voice.
newsitem.headline: French Snow White sues Disney for "stolen" voice.

text.p: An actress who dubbed Snow White into French sued the Walt Disney Company on Thursday, charging it had failed to pay her royalties on videos of the film and records of its sound track.
Lucie Dolene, 66, who sang the French version of the song "One Day my Prince will Come", told a Paris court the company had "stolen her voice".
She demanded half a million francs ($100,000) in damages under a 1985 French law protecting artists' copyrights.
Lawyers for the Walt Disney company said the terms of Dolene's hiring in 1958 allowed for later use of her voice. They said the 1985 law could not be used retroactively.
The court will deliver its ruling on December 6.
Dolene told Reuters she dubbed "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs" in one week for 5,000 francs ($1,000) at the time.
She said she was still working and recently dubbed the speaking tea-pot in the Walt Disney cartoon "Beauty and the Beast".
